```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Define a function to create a ggplot
plot_with_color <- function(data, x_var, y_var, color_var) {
  ggplot(data, aes_string(x = x_var, y = y_var, color = color_var)) +
    geom_point() +
    theme_minimal()
}

# Example usage with the built-in 'mtcars' dataset
plot_with_color(mtcars, "mpg", "hp", "cyl")

```
```{r}
#install.packages("gganimate")
#install.packages("ggplot2") # If you haven't installed ggplot2 yet
library(ggplot2)
library(gganimate)
library(tidyverse)
```
```{r}
# Create a sample dataset
data <- data.frame(
  id = 1:10,
  x1 = rnorm(10, mean = 0, sd = 1),
  y1 = rnorm(10, mean = 0, sd = 1),
  x2 = rnorm(10, mean = 2, sd = 1),
  y2 = rnorm(10, mean = 2, sd = 1)
)

```

```{r}
# Reshape the data for animation
library(tidyr)

data_long <- data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("x"),
               names_to = "dimension",
               names_prefix = "x",
               values_to = "x") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("y"),
               names_to = "dimension_y",
               names_prefix = "y",
               values_to = "y") %>%
  filter(dimension == dimension_y) %>%
  mutate(dimension = factor(dimension))

```

```{r}
# Create the animated plot
animated_plot <- ggplot(data_long, aes(x = x, y = y, group = id)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, aes(color = as.factor(id))) +
  theme_minimal() +
  transition_states(dimension, transition_length = 2, state_length = 1) +
  ease_aes('cubic-in-out') +
  labs(title = "Transition between two dimensions")

# Render the animation
animate(animated_plot, nframes = 100, fps = 10)

```
